Commit message needs update for tested section. Other changes lgtm.
I think explicit check to verify type for TCP will enable us to add more types in future. In else condition we can throw exception.
Acknowledged

Can we save ResponderInfo instead of inventoryPath?
Also generate the deviceName whenever needed ??
Acknowledged

Even if we need the name (I can't understand why we would , especially since we have the object path) - Naming strategy here seems to be weak. Neither the eid nor the ipaddress are not globally unique identities.

In the current OpenBMC codebase, the MCTP daemon implementation follows a design in which the BMC acts as the bus owner and is responsible for assigning EIDs to all downstream devices. During EID assignment, the BMC ensures that each EID is unique across the system, even when the same physical device is reachable through multiple transport interfaces such as PCIe and I2C.


We can not take the object path as it is - as object path belongs to the discovery object path eg /au/com/codeconstruct/mctp1/networks/1/endpoints/9

Second reason to choose the EID/IPaddress is for the readability.
What do you want to keep it for the TCP discovery - hostname/ipaddress.
I don't have any issues with either.

> In the current OpenBMC codebase, the MCTP daemon implementation follows a design in which the BMC acts as the bus owner and is responsible for assigning EIDs to all downstream devices. During EID assignment, the BMC ensures that each EID is unique across the system, even when the same physical device is reachable through multiple transport interfaces such as PCIe and I2C.

But , what if the MCTP implementation change ? Technically as per the spec its totally allowed to have same EID across multiple networks. And from this change, i am not understanding why we need device name ? because this patch does not consume it. is this purely needed for debugging ? or do we plan to use it for something later in your patches ? If it is for debugging I think we should purely drop it because redfish endpoints should clearly show the links between component intergrity and actually physical device already right ?

The impact will be much higher if if the MCTP implementation change.
> i am not understanding why we need device name
With the current change, the D-Bus object name will use the EID as its identifier. In a subsequent commit, we plan to retrieve the inventory object name from the Entity Manager using the EID and use that instead. The following commit contains the initial implementation of this approach, but it requires rebasing and further rework:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/spdm/+/83262/1/requester/mctp_transport_discovery.cpp

so , when you say , "identifier" you mean its the leaf node in the dbus object path. I think this entire thing needs to go in a commit that uses it & I wish we had captured the intent a bit more elaborately in the commit message. That a side, I don't think we need to complicate this by adding device name. Can't we just have simple incremental numbering for dbus objects like (1,2,..) and let `associations` on the object tell which device it really is ?

> we plan to retrieve the inventory object name from the Entity Manager using the EID and use that instead.

I just saw the other commit its like 6-7 commits above this one.  I am not sure how many things would change as we move from a commit to another as we go through the review process. I think this probably have a chance if it moves to the commit that uses it.

Yes, there will be additional commits on top of this one. Immediately after this commit, we need to implement the interfaces (ComponentIntegrity and TrustedInterface). For that, we need the D-Bus objects in place, and those objects will require names.

Currently, the object names will be based on the EIDs of the MCTP-discovered objects. Later, we plan to replace those EID-based names with the corresponding inventory object names. So this commit is required now because the next commit depends on it. I can have the follow-up commit ready as well.

I'm not sure why we're blocked on the naming of the D-Bus object path, especially since the current naming is intended as an intermediate step and will be updated once the inventory object names become available.

When the EM config patch comes in(https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/spdm/+/83262/1) we have D-Bus objects populated like this
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/BMC_0
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/CPU_0

This steps is intermediate step to show EID(MCTP) or IP Addrress(TCP) till then so that E2E attestation can be verified. 
Ex:
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/20
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/30

@ratan, @chinmay -  Over the past few years in OpenBMC, we've intentionally moved away from encoding meaning into D-Bus object paths. Instead, we rely on associations to derive the relationships and semantics. Ideally, an object path should be treated as an opaque identifier rather than something consumers parse to infer meaning.I'm fully in favor of using a meaningful and unique name where appropriate. However, neither the EID nor the IP address can be considered globally unique identifiers, so using them in the object path doesn't solve the uniqueness problem.For that reason, I would like to see a simple unique naming (may be a sequential numbering like 1,2,3..) until we have the EM support. I don't think I can merge this change in its current form.> This steps is intermediate step to show EID(MCTP) or IP Addrress(TCP) till then so that E2E attestation can be verified.There is no code in the upstream repository currently to do en E2E testing. I am not sure how having EID & TCP IP on the dbus object would help.

> This steps is intermediate step to show EID(MCTP) or IP Addrress(TCP) till then so that E2E attestation can be verified.

There is no code in the upstream repository currently to do en E2E testing. I am not sure how having EID & TCP IP on the dbus object would help.

--> Sorry, I didn’t mean redfish — I meant using the D-Bus API with busctl calls in this commit chain (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/spdm/+/84019/13)

If concern for using EID till we have EM support is because there could be duplicate EID on different network?. In that case we can see if we can use network id and eid as an intermediate approach till we have EM support. 

Entity Manager maintains the mapping from EID to the inventory object. However, if the concern is that we'll be making decisions based on the object name, that's not the case. We'll use the associated MCTP object to retrieve the EID and base the decision on that instead.

When we have EM changes in, SPDM daemon does a mapping for EID and inventory with the association present in EM to get a device name

With modified patch in current MR object path for spdm will be /xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/1_20
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/1_30

With EM change it will be
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/CPU_0
/xyz/openbmc_project/component_integrity/CPU_1


BMCWeb does one mapper call for component integrity to fetch objects implementing ComponentIntegrityInterface. Similar to FW inventory where it looks for objects implementing version interface. Id property in ComponentIntegrity redfish will use objectpath.filename()

Later for links in component integrity and trusted components we need couple of more association, for reporting and authenticating association.
Updated the patch to use network id + eid for device name for object path until EM changes available
we can have same endpoints id's across multiple MCTP networks. why not UUID ?

Partially responded above, UUID is a random number for each device on the system and we will never know that this UUID is belongs to which device until and unless someone goes and read the machine book and do this mapping.
EID is done by the BMC and will be same for the platform.

*As explained above in the current mctpd implementation: the BMC ensures that each EID is unique across the system, even when the same physical device is reachable through multiple transport interfaces such as PCIe and I2C.*

We could have add the physical medium in the object name but not needed now, we can do it later once we hit this issue.
It would be better to add this function in the same commit where it is used.
line no 18 on this file, where it is used.
what's the need for deriving different names for MCTP and TCP ? we already have the dbus object path of the responder from the discovery phase.
